messages:
sam: Heads up — running into TLS handshake failures when our Python SDK (sync + async) talks to Dedicated through a corporate HTTP proxy + custom CA. Works fine with curl pointing at the same CA bundle, but the SDK raises: `ssl.SSLError: [SSL: TLSV1_ALERT_UNKNOWN_CA] tlsv1 alert unknown ca`

sam: Minimal reproducer in the sample app (using the SDK client):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(base_url=\"https://private.redwood.example\", api_key=API_KEY)
resp = client.generate(prompt=\"hi\")
print(resp.text)
```

sam: Environment: Debian container, company forward proxy set via `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`, custom CA at `/etc/ssl/certs/company.pem`. I tried `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/company.pem` and `SSL_CERT_FILE` but only curl honors it. Requests-based calls from other apps pick it up though.

jon: @sam do you have `verify` being overridden anywhere in our SDK wrappers? We pass `verify` through to requests/urllib3. If base_url is a non-standard hostname or we do SNI rewriting inside proxy, that could break.

sam: I grepped — SDK calls `Session()` then `session.request(...)` without forcing `verify` param. My expectation was env vars would be respected by requests, but the proxy path may be doing CONNECT then presenting a different cert chain. Stack trace snippet:
```
File \"/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/urllib3/connectionpool.py\", line 699, in _validate_conn
  conn.connect()
File \"/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/urllib3/connection.py\", line 420, in connect
  cert = self.sock.getpeercert(binary_form=True)
ssl.SSLError: [SSL: TLSV1_ALERT_UNKNOWN_CA] tlsv1 alert unknown ca
```

maria: Two quick checks: 1) is the SDK using `certifi` bundle explicitly (that can override env vars)? 2) are we switching HTTP client libraries in async path (aiohttp) that don't read `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`?

sam: Good point — sync path uses requests, async path uses aiohttp via `aiohttp.ClientSession` in our async client. I noticed the async client earlier didn't accept a `ca_certs` parameter. That might explain why async fails even when sync sometimes works.

taylor: This is two related issues: user experience for Dedicated/private base_url + proxies (docs/sample app) and an SDK bug/feature gap for passing custom CA bundles through both sync and async clients. I filed a quick GH issue: #3245 (dx: allow `ca_bundle` arg and env fallback).

sam: Also found an oddity: when base_url includes a port (e.g., `https://private.redwood.example:8443/`) our internal proxy rewrites Host header and requests' poolmanager uses a different connection key, which seems to bypass OS-level CA lookup in our container image. Repro is flaky.

jon: For the immediate workaround, can you try forcing `session.verify = '/etc/ssl/certs/company.pem'` before calling `request()` in the sample? If that fixes sync, it's a clear path: expose `verify` on the SDK client's init and document for Dedicated users behind intercepting proxies.

sam: I tried that — sync passes. Async still fails because aiohttp needs `ssl=ssl_context` on the session. Example I used:
```python
import ssl, aiohttp
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=\"/etc/ssl/certs/company.pem\")
session = aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=ctx))
```

maria: So feature request: SDK should accept `ca_bundle` (path) or `ssl_context` and wire it into both clients, plus fall back to `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`/`SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR` if provided. Also add docs for Dedicated: proxy env var caveats and examples for sync/async.

taylor: Agree. Bonus: add a quick sample app in `examples/dedicated-proxy/` showing `HTTP_PROXY` + `ca_bundle` usage and a Dockerfile that copies company CA into image. That should reduce onboarding friction.

jon: Typing/UX note: make `ca_bundle` param typed as `Optional[str]` and accept `ssl.SSLContext` too. For the async client signature: `async def __init__(..., ca_bundle: Optional[Union[str, ssl.SSLContext]] = None)` and keep runtime checks. We need stubs updated in `typeshed` or our own py.typed.

taylor: Also check retry/auth behavior: when we do a 307 redirect or proxy auth, some HTTP clients drop Authorization header on cross-host redirects. We should ensure our internal retry logic reattaches bearer tokens for same-origin or follow a safe policy. Add tests for proxy auth header preservation.

sam: One more hiccup: Windows devs reported the SDK ignoring the Windows cert store even when `certifi` isn't present. We should document platform differences and prefer explicit `ca_bundle` param for deterministic behavior.

infra-bot: deploy-log: example-service (staging) build #4527 — no TLS errors after applying `session.verify` workaround on image build.

maria: Ok next steps I can take: 1) PR to add `ca_bundle` + `ssl_context` plumbing for sync/async (including types + tests), 2) update examples + docs, 3) add an integration test with a proxy+fake-CA. Can someone help with a simple reproducible proxy connector?

jon: I can spin up a tiny mitmproxy container in the CI matrix and add it to the integration job. Will pair on the test.

sam: Thanks — filing follow-ups in GH and will paste links here when ready. For now the workaround notes are: set `session.verify` for sync; create `ssl.SSLContext` and pass into `aiohttp.TCPConnector` for async; ensure container image installs company CA at a path you pass in.

maria: Thanks everyone. This should get our Dedicated private customers unblocked and improve DX. :thumbsup:
